clue.text: One with cracking art who could get deco?

definitions.text: One with cracking art who could get deco?

parts.words: One with cracking art who could get deco?
parts.note: cracking codes is the art; and if you break up the word code itself you can get deco

explanation.surface: A puzzle about someone skilled at cracking, wondering whether they could achieve an Art Deco look.
explanation.walkthrough: Two readings: a CODEBREAKER cracks ciphers, and breaking the letters of CODE rearranges them into DECO.
explanation.definitionFit: A codebreaker is a cryptanalyst, whose skill is cracking ciphers.

clue.text: See you support 'X'?

parts.note: to cheer a team is to support it
X is the Roman numeral ten, written 10, which looks like the letters IO

explanation.surface: A farewell paired with a cheer for someone called X, or a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: X is ten, and 10 written out looks like the letters IO.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerio is an informal British goodbye, the same parting phrase as see you.

clue.text: Dull, dreary, dingy, depressing … D is the initial sign of misery, all unending

indicators.note: the initial sign of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of misery

indicators.note: unending means the last letter of all is cut off

parts.note: all without its end

explanation.surface: A gloomy string of D-words, then a lesson that D stands for misery.
explanation.walkthrough: The list of D-words reads like a definition run-on; the wordplay is D, IS, M (the initial of misery) and AL (all without its final L).
explanation.definitionFit: Dismal describes something gloomy and cheerless, matching every one of the listed synonyms.

clue.text: Worker who might put on two pairs of shoes

definitions.text: Worker who might put on two pairs of shoes

parts.words: Worker who might put on two pairs of shoes
parts.note: a horse has four hooves, so it is given two pairs of shoes by a farrier at the forge

explanation.surface: A worker dressing themselves in two pairs of shoes at once.
explanation.walkthrough: The shoes are horseshoes, nailed onto a horse's four hooves, not worn by the worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A smith who forges iron traditionally makes and fits horseshoes on a horse's hooves.

clue.text: Extra accessible solve you'd set for beginners?

definitions.text: Extra accessible solve you'd set for beginners?

indicators.note: beginners are the opening letters of the words before them

parts.note: first letter of Extra
first letter of accessible
first letter of solve
first letter of you'd

explanation.surface: A setter promising a particularly accessible puzzle for novices.
explanation.walkthrough: The beginnings of the first four words spell the answer, and the whole clue describes it too.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy puzzle is simple, the sort a setter pitches at novice solvers.

clue.text: Want to get aboard, carry on wading

indicators.note: getting aboard means going inside, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: to keep is to carry on
to want is to need

explanation.surface: Someone eager to board a boat keeps going through the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wading is in water reaching up to the knees, an adjectival sense of the compound.

clue.text: Fashionable rival hosts love Italy's pasta

indicators.note: to host is to hold a guest inside
to fashion is to shape, so the letters of rival are reshaped

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A trendy competitor entertains, serving Italian pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli are small filled parcels of pasta.

clue.text: Plant and flower ultimately having cut prices — excellent on the counter

indicators.note: the letter cuts into the word, sitting inside it

parts.note: fees are prices charged

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter

parts.note: last letter of flower

indicators.note: counter means going against, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written AI

explanation.surface: A florist's shop with a plant and flowers, cut prices and a fine display on the counter.
explanation.walkthrough: R (the end of flower) cuts into FEES; then AI (A1, excellent) reversed by 'on the counter' gives IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Freesia is a fragrant flowering plant from southern Africa grown from corms.

clue.text: Bakery sticks with francs?

parts.note: the long sticks sold at a bakery, which you would buy with francs in France

explanation.surface: A bakery that keeps accepting the old French currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sticks' looks like a verb; it is the noun for long loaves, and francs place them in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Baguettes, the long thin loaves, are commonly called this in English.

clue.text: What could be in the cupboard — mothballs?

definitions.text: What could be in the cupboard
definitions.meaning: first meaning: ledges fitted inside a cupboard
second meaning: puts aside or postpones, as a project is mothballed

explanation.walkthrough: Mothballs sit in a cupboard in the surface, but here the word is a verb for postponing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the plural noun for storage ledges and the verb for setting plans aside indefinitely.

clue.text: Broadcast of Sonny & Cher is set at the same time

indicators.note: broadcasting scatters something widely, so these letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Sonny & Cher show is aired simultaneously.
explanation.walkthrough: Sonny & Cher were a 1960s-70s American pop duo.
explanation.definitionFit: To synchronise watches is to set them so they agree at the same moment.

clue.text: Unopened kit characterises reserves

indicators.note: unopened means the first letter is removed

parts.note: gear is kit, equipment
to mark something is to characterise it

explanation.surface: Sealed kit identifies the reserve players.
explanation.definitionFit: To earmark funds is to set them aside for a purpose, as reserving does.

clue.text: Little woman breaks up row begun by a neighbour

indicators.note: breaking up the word means splitting it so another sits inside

parts.note: a din is a row, a loud noise
Jo is one of the sisters in Little Women

explanation.surface: A small woman stops a quarrel started by the person next door.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Women is Louisa May Alcott's novel about the March sisters, Jo among them.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs, to adjoin something is to border it, lying next to it.

clue.text: With four-fifths of poll, upcoming turn in charge for me?

definitions.text: With four-fifths of poll, upcoming turn in charge for me?

indicators.note: four of the five letters are kept, the last dropped

parts.note: a count of votes is a poll

indicators.note: in a down clue upcoming means read from the bottom up

parts.note: a roll is a turn

explanation.surface: A candidate with 80% of the vote expects a turn in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: COUN (COUNT less its last letter) then ROLL and IC read upwards as CILLOR; the whole clue is the elected official's own thought.
explanation.definitionFit: A councillor is an elected member of a local council, taking a turn in office after winning votes.

clue.text: Student in bed using dope? On the contrary

indicators.note: in places the student within the bed

parts.note: a cot is a bed
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student lying in bed takes drugs, or the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' flips 'Student in bed using dope': the dope is what uses, or is made of, a student in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A clot is a stupid person, the same informal insult as dope.

clue.text: Keep reduced portion of shrimp over — I shared

indicators.note: portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone sharing out a helping of shrimp and offering the leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: To impoverish someone is to make them poor, keeping their means diminished.

clue.text: Criminal court locking up bishop over street stall

indicators.note: locking up means holding inside
criminal suggests a crooked version of the word court
in a down clue one piece sits over the next

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A criminal court jails a bishop over a street market stall.
explanation.definitionFit: To obstruct is to block or hinder, as stalling does.

clue.text: Gossip takes part in promotion

indicators.note: in puts the part inside the promotion

parts.note: backing is support or promotion
a bit is a part

explanation.surface: A tattler joins in a publicity campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Backbiting is spiteful talk about someone behind their back, malicious gossip.

clue.text: Hanging in the bag, uniform needed for Spain

indicators.note: one letter is needed in place of another, a swap

parts.note: in the bag means certain, assured
E is the international vehicle code for Spain
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Packing a uniform for a trip to Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtain is a piece of fabric hung at a window, a hanging.

clue.text: Resounding item often used by 1 Across

definitions.text: Resounding item often used by 1 Across

parts.words: Resounding item often used by 1 Across
parts.note: a resounding repeat of sound, and also the NATO name for the commonest letter in English, which a cipher cracker leans on

explanation.surface: A reverberation that a cipher expert finds useful.
explanation.walkthrough: Frequency analysis starts with E, the most common English letter, and Echo is E's NATO alphabet name.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a reflected sound that resounds back to the listener.

clue.text: Hundreds taking in rugby when Italy finally could get Slam

indicators.note: taking in means holding within

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral hundred, so two hundreds are CC
RU is rugby union
if can mean when, as in if it rains

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter

parts.note: last letter of Italy

explanation.surface: Italy hope to win a rugby Grand Slam, finally.
explanation.walkthrough: A Grand Slam in the Six Nations is winning every match; here slam means criticise.
explanation.definitionFit: To crucify someone in the press is to criticise them savagely, an informal sense of slam.

clue.text: Tango with flower girl spinning about around partner

indicators.note: around has the reversed name placed outside the letter for about
spinning turns the girl's name round so it reads backwards

parts.note: Rose is a girl's name and a flower
C is circa, about
T is tango in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A tango dancer whirls with a flower girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinning' turns ROSE into ESOR, which goes 'around' C (circa, about) to give ESCOR; the T of Tango joins on to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: An escort is a companion who accompanies someone, a partner at an event.

clue.text: Flaws of traitor spotted in time

indicators.note: spotted in means found inside

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is a traitor

explanation.surface: Weaknesses of a betrayer are noticed promptly.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are errors in a printed work, mistakes listed for correction.

clue.text: State of teacher, maybe the one instructing us?

parts.note: pupils address a female teacher as Miss
our means belonging to us
I is one as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A query about the condition of the teacher who instructs the class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State of' reads as condition, but State is the definition; the rest is 'Miss, our I(nstructor)'.
explanation.definitionFit: Missouri is a US state in the Midwest.

clue.text: Adult human female's complaint when we're instructed: Don't use 'mother'

indicators.note: don't use tells the solver to leave this out

parts.note: a malady is an illness, a complaint
Ma is mother

explanation.surface: A woman's protest at being told not to call anyone mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady is a woman, the polite term for a grown female person.

clue.text: Something posted about Hollywood suppressing Universal movie

indicators.note: suppressing has the city sitting on the letter, placed next to it
about means turned around so the word is backwards

parts.note: a card is something posted
U is the film certificate for universal
LA, Los Angeles, is home to Hollywood

explanation.surface: A mailed card about Hollywood hushing up a Universal Studios film.
explanation.walkthrough: Universal Pictures made the 1931 film of the vampire tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Dracula is the title of the classic vampire film, so a movie.

clue.text: Sidle on in elegantly, circling like a cat

indicators.note: the surrounding words circle the answer, holding it within them

parts.note: the letters straddle the words from sidle to elegantly

explanation.surface: Slinking in gracefully, prowling around like a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonine means lion-like, and a lion is a big cat.

clue.text: Dope Tony's knocked out on, abrasive basic stuff

parts.note: a nit is a fool, a dope

indicators.note: knocked out means removed

parts.note: the name as written
gritty means rough, abrasive

explanation.surface: An idiot called Tony is floored, rough stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: The nitty-gritty is the fundamental core of a matter, its essentials.
